title: Per-model precision policy horizon, calibration campaign, and fail-safe constraints
creator: Asha Menon
description: Establish a reproducible per-model precision policy (recommended precision profile and operational guardrails) and run a calibration + validation campaign to populate the model catalog with safe defaults for FP8 and INT8. Deliverables: recommendation engine for profile selection, calibration harness for representative samples, CI gating rules, and a staged rollout plan with automatic failover to higher-precision variants.
background: Customers running models in Dedicated and Private deployments ask for safe, opinionated precision choices to reduce cost without unexpected accuracy regressions. Prior work has produced quant presets and calibration helpers, but we lack an automated policy that selects a precision profile per model variant and tests the profile against canonical eval sets under CI and shadow traffic.
goals: 1) Define a decision surface that maps model metadata + workload fingerprint to a recommended precision profile (FP8 variant or INT8 with per-channel weights). 2) Implement a calibration campaign that produces calibration artifacts and metrics for the catalog. 3) Create CI gates and runtime guardrails to prevent rollouts that cause unacceptable regressions.
non_goals: 1) Implementing a full auto-quant compiler end-to-end (we will call existing compiler infra). 2) Changing model training pipelines. 3) Wide re-training to recover precision-induced regressions.
success_metrics: Catalog coverage: recommended profile available for >= 90% of models in the open catalog
Accuracy regressions: relative degradation vs FP16 baseline < 0.7% (task-dependent threshold) on canonical evals
Cost reduction: median per-token cost reduction >= 25% for INT8, >= 40% for FP8 where applicable
Rollout safety: no production rollback caused by quant-related quality regression in the first 30 days of this rollout
proposed_solution: Build a lightweight recommendation engine that ingests model metadata (architecture, size, activation ranges, historical sequence length distribution) and proposes candidate profiles: 'FP16-safe', 'FP8-eager', 'INT8-conservative', plus per-op overrides. For each candidate, run an automated calibration job that produces quantization parameters, simulated end-to-end inference runs on canonical eval sets, and a regression report. Persist artifacts to the catalog and annotate the model entry with recommended profile and confidence band.
calibration_workflow: 1) Sample selection: use the model's fingerprinting service to select an N=500 sample set stratified by sequence length and input token distribution. 2) Calibration methods: run A) min-max + percentile clipping, B) KL divergence histogram calibration, and C) MSE per-channel for weights. 3) Calibration batch settings: minibatch size 8, 1024 tokens per sample budget. 4) Evaluate each calibration artifact by running the calibrated model on canonical eval sets and compute delta metrics vs FP16 baseline. 5) Produce a single chosen artifact per profile with metadata: method, dataset hash, version, delta metrics, and confidence band.
validation_plan: 1) Define canonical eval suites per task family (LM completion, QA EM/F1, summarization ROUGE, translation BLEU, embeddings cosine similarity). 2) For each model and candidate profile run: baseline FP16 -> quantized run -> compute task-specific metrics. 3) Acceptance criteria: absolute metric delta < task-specific threshold (examples: QA EM <0.5 absolute, ROUGE-L <1.0 absolute, BLEU <1.0 absolute, embeddings cosine drop <0.005). 4) Statistical checks: bootstrap confidence intervals and signed-rank test to ensure differences are significant. 5) Store evaluation artifacts and a one-page regression summary in the catalog entry.
rollout_plan: 1) Shadow phase: deploy quantized variant in shadow mode for 72h on 5% of traffic, capture token-level traces and user-level metrics. 2) Canary: 10% traffic for 24h with active comparison vs same-serving baseline route. 3) Gradual ramp: 25% -> 50% -> 100% with automated checks at each step. 4) Automatic fallback: if monitored metric breach occurs (see guardrails) the system automatically switches traffic back to the pinned FP16 variant and opens an incident ticket.
ci_and_gating: 1) CI job 'quant-calibrate' runs on PRs that affect quant infra. 2) Unit checks: quant ops parity smoke tests. 3) Integration: run simplified canonical evals in CI (subset) and require regression < threshold. 4) Release gating: a model catalog publish requires 'calibration report' artifact and 'quality_stamp: pass' for the recommended profile. 5) Binary gating: if any profile causes >=1.5% relative regression on any critical metric, block catalog publish.
monitoring_and_telemetry: Emit the following time-series for quantized variants: per-token latency, tokens-per-second, cost-per-token estimate, delta_metric_vs_fp16, quantization_overflow_rate, activation-saturation-rate, and sample-level divergence histograms. Add a catalog dashboard tile showing profile, confidence band, calibration method, and last-run timestamp.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Calibration sample bias leads to poor real-world perf. Mitigation: stratified sampling + reserve 'wildcard' samples from live traffic for second-stage validation.

Risk: Over-eager FP8 recommendations cause hallucinations or factual errors. Mitigation: conservative default thresholds for knowledge-sensitive tasks; require additional manual review for models tagged 'high-fidelity' or 'safety-sensitive'.
Risk: CI runtime cost becomes large. Mitigation: run full evals nightly and lightweight checks on PRs; cache calibration artifacts and reuse where model metadata identical.
open_decisions: Decision: threshold numbers for task-specific acceptance criteria (exact deltas). Pending PM + Eval team confirmation.
Decision: storage TTL for calibration artifacts in catalog (default 90 days vs permanent).
Decision: whether FP8 E5M2 vs E4M3 notation and mapping should be exposed in public catalog UI.
